message.content:
Here’s a quick guide on how to pull the CNAME records for **sample.com** via the VirusTotal v3 API and then extract just the related object IDs.

---

## 1. Make the API request

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "secret123"          # <-- keep this private!
DOMAIN   = "sample.com"

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns_records"
params = {"type": "CNAME"}     # filter to only CNAME records
headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
    "Accept": "application/json"
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
data = response.json()
```

> **Endpoint used:**  
> `GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}/dns_records?type=CNAME`

---

## 2. Extract the related object IDs

The JSON payload will look something like this (simplified):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "dns_record_id_1",
      "attributes": { ... }
    },
    {
      "id": "dns_record_id_2",
      "attributes": { ... }
    }
  ]
}
```

To pull just the IDs:

```python
ids = [record["id"] for record in data.get("data", [])]
print(ids)   # e.g., ['dns_record_id_1', 'dns_record_id_2']
```

---

### Full example

```python
import requests

def get_cname_ids(domain, api_key):
    url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}/dns_records"
    params = {"type": "CNAME"}
    headers = {"x-apikey": api_key, "Accept": "application/json"}

    resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
    resp.raise_for_status()          # raise an error if the request failed
    data = resp.json()

    return [rec["id"] for rec in data.get("data", [])]

# Usage
cname_ids = get_cname_ids("sample.com", "secret123")
print(cname_ids)
```

That’s all you need—just replace `"secret123"` with your real key and run the script. The output will be a list of the CNAME record IDs associated with `sample.com`.
